extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers learning first-order logic (readers of a mathematical logic textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines, syntactic conditions, axioms, and metatheorems for constructing and verifying deductions in a first-order deductive calculus (including substitutability, axiom groups, generalization, deduction, soundness, and equality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutability of a term for a variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: 't is substitutable for x in α' is given recursively: (1) For atomic α, t is always substitutable for x in α. (2) t is substitutable for x in (¬ α) iff it is substitutable for x in α. t is substitutable for x in (α → β) iff it is substitutable for x in both α and β. (3) t is substitutable for x in ∀ y α iff either (a) x does not occur free in ∀ y α, or (b) y does not occur in t and t is substitutable for x in α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: prevent capture of variables by quantifiers when forming α_x^t. Examples and cautions: x is always substitutable for itself; if t contains no variables that occur in α then t is substitutable for x in α. Even if t is not substitutable, α_x^t is still syntactically formed by replacing free occurrences of x by t, but such substitutions may produce ill-behaved sentences (quantifier capture). Use recursive definition for proofs by induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom group 2 (quantifier axiom schema)
rubrics_metrics.description: Axiom group 2 consists of all generalizations of formulas of the form ∀ x α → α_x^t, where the term t is substitutable for the variable x in the formula α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: formalizes the intended meaning of the universal quantifier (if α holds of everything then it holds of t) but only when substitutability prevents capture. Examples: ∀ v3( ∀ v1(Av1 → ∀ v2 Av2) → (Av2 → ∀ v2 Av2)) is in axiom group 2; ∀ v1 ∀ v2 Bv1v2 → ∀ v2 Bv2v2 is not because v2 is not substitutable for v1 in ∀ v2 Bv1v2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom group 1 (tautologies as logical axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Axiom group 1 consists of generalizations of tautologies of sentential logic (using only ¬ and →) obtained by replacing each sentence symbol by a wff of the first-order language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative view: treat prime formulas (atomic or of form ∀ x α) as propositional atoms and include all propositional tautologies over those atoms. Remarks: taking all tautologies is overkill but gives a decidable set useful for enumerability; one could instead choose a smaller decidable subset and derive others by modus ponens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization Theorem (conditions for introducing ∀)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ ⊢ ϕ and x does not occur free in any formula in Γ, then Γ ⊢ ∀ x ϕ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: prove by induction that the set {ϕ | Γ ⊢ ∀ x ϕ} contains Γ and the logical axioms and is closed under modus ponens; axiom groups 3 and 4 are needed for the inductive step. The restriction that x not occur free in Γ is essential (counterexamples exist otherwise). The proof also yields an effective transformation of a deduction of ϕ into a deduction of ∀ x ϕ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule T (Lemma 24C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ ⊢ α1, ..., Γ ⊢ αn and {α1, ..., αn} tautologically implies β, then Γ ⊢ β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: the formula α1 → ··· → αn → β is a tautology and hence a logical axiom; apply modus ponens n times. Used to combine previously obtained theorems when they tautologically imply another formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ; γ ⊢ ϕ, then Γ ⊢ (γ → ϕ). (Conversely, modus ponens yields the reverse direction.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two proofs: (1) semantic via compactness/tautological implication; (2) syntactic by induction transforming a deduction of ϕ from Γ; γ into a deduction of γ → ϕ from Γ using Rule T and closure properties. Use as a standard tool to convert assumptions into antecedents in implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraposition (Corollary 24D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ; ϕ ⊢ ¬ ψ iff Γ; ψ ⊢ ¬ ϕ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the deduction theorem and Rule T: from Γ; ϕ ⊢ ¬ ψ get Γ ⊢ ϕ → ¬ ψ and since ϕ → ¬ ψ tautologically implies ψ → ¬ ϕ, apply Rule T to get Γ ⊢ ψ → ¬ ϕ, hence Γ; ψ ⊢ ¬ ϕ. Use symmetry for the converse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reductio ad absurdum (Corollary 24E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ; ϕ is inconsistent (i.e., for some β both β and ¬ β are theorems of Γ; ϕ), then Γ ⊢ ¬ ϕ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: from Γ; ϕ inconsistency obtain Γ ⊢ (ϕ → β) and Γ ⊢ (ϕ → ¬ β). The set {ϕ → β, ϕ → ¬ β} tautologically implies ¬ ϕ, so by Rule T Γ ⊢ ¬ ϕ. Use RAA as a strategy when direct methods fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntactic strategy for finding deductions (case analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: When attempting to show Γ ⊢ ϕ, consider the syntactic form of ϕ and proceed by cases: (1) If ϕ is (ψ → θ) then show Γ; ψ ⊢ θ. (2) If ϕ is ∀ x ψ and x not free in Γ, then show Γ ⊢ ψ (or use re-replacement lemma). (3) If ϕ is a negation, handle subcases: (3a) ϕ = ¬(ψ → θ) show Γ ⊢ ψ and Γ ⊢ ¬ θ; (3b) ϕ = ¬¬ψ show Γ ⊢ ψ; (3c) ϕ = ¬ ∀ x ψ try to show Γ ⊢ ¬ ψ_x^t for some substitutable term t or use contraposition/RAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backward reasoning is frequently useful; use deduction/generalization/contraposition/RAA to reduce the goal to simpler subgoals. The text gives the worked example ∃ x ∀ y ϕ → ∀ y ∃ x ϕ showing the sequence of reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization on constants (Theorem 24F and Corollary 24G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ ⊢ ϕ and c is a constant symbol not occurring in Γ, then there is a variable y (not occurring in ϕ) such that Γ ⊢ ∀ y ϕ_c^y, and there is a deduction of ∀ y ϕ_c^y from Γ in which c does not occur. Corollary: if Γ ⊢ ϕ_x^c with c new, then Γ ⊢ ∀ x ϕ (provided substitutability/re-replacement conditions hold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: replace occurrences of c by a fresh variable y throughout a deduction of ϕ to obtain a deduction of ϕ_c^y without c, then apply generalization. Useful to move from a derivation that uses a fresh constant to a universal statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existential Instantiation (Rule EI, Corollary 24H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume constant symbol c does not occur in ϕ, ψ, or Γ, and Γ; ϕ_x^c ⊢ ψ. Then Γ; ∃ x ϕ ⊢ ψ, and there is a deduction of ψ from Γ; ∃ x ϕ in which c does not occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: if from assumption 'ϕ with a fresh constant c in place of x' you can prove ψ, then from ∃ x ϕ you can prove ψ. Note: Rule EI does not assert ∃ x ϕ ⊢ ϕ_x^c (this is generally false). Use contraposition and generalization in the provided proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of alphabetic variants (Theorem 24I)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any formula ϕ, term t, and variable x, one can find an alphabetic variant ϕ' (differing from ϕ only in choice of bound variables) such that (a) ϕ ↔ ϕ' are mutually deducible (ϕ ⊢ ϕ' and ϕ' ⊢ ϕ), and (b) t is substitutable for x in ϕ'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: recursively rename bound variables where necessary (choose fresh z not occurring in ϕ' or t) to avoid capture and make t substitutable. Use this when an initial substitution fails due to variable capture; replace with logically equivalent variant where substitution is legal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality axioms and requirements (Eq1–Eq5)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of properties required about equality in the language containing '=': Eq1: ⊢ ∀ x x = x (reflexivity). Eq2: ⊢ ∀ x ∀ y(x = y → y = x) (symmetry). Eq3: ⊢ ∀ x ∀ y ∀ z(x = y → y = z → x = z) (transitivity). Eq4 (predicates): for n-place predicate P, ⊢ ∀ x1 ... ∀ xn ∀ y1 ... ∀ yn (x1=y1 → ... → xn=yn → (P x1...xn → P y1...yn)). Eq5 (functions): for n-place function f, ⊢ ∀ x1 ... ∀ xn ∀ y1 ... ∀ yn (x1=y1 → ... → xn=yn → f x1...xn = f y1...yn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: equality is an equivalence relation and is compatible with predicate and function symbols. Proofs use axiom group 5 (reflexivity) and axiom group 6 schemata (compatibility). These are minimal axioms sufficient to derive the usual properties of equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution lemma (semantic correctness of substitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 25B: For assignment s and term u, s(u_x^t) = s(x | s(t))(u). Substitution Lemma: If term t is substitutable for x in formula ϕ, then |=_A ϕ_x^t [s] iff |=_A ϕ [ s(x | s(t)) ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning: performing a syntactic substitution inside a term/formula corresponds semantically to changing the assignment. This lemma underlies the correctness of axiom group 2 (∀x α → α_x^t) and is used in the semantic proof of soundness. Proofs proceed by induction on the term/formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness Theorem requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ ⊢ ϕ, then Γ |= ϕ (every deducible formula is logically valid relative to the premises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: show every logical axiom is valid (Lemma 25A) and that modus ponens preserves validity; then induct on length of deductions. For axiom groups this requires checking tautologies, quantifier axioms (via substitution lemma), equality axioms, etc. Ensures deductions only produce semantically correct conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of backward reasoning and meta-level proofs for constructing formal deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique: give an informal (English) proof that truth of Γ implies truth of ϕ, then formalize that proof into a legal deduction. Also, use backward strategies (reduce goal to smaller subgoals) and syntactic transformations (deduction theorem, generalization, contraposition, RAA, re-replacement/alphabetic variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: exhaustive enumeration of finite sequences is effective but impractical; instead, employ the described case analyses and transformations to systematically construct deductions. Several worked examples illustrate how to compress pedigree trees into linear deductions and how to reuse deductions by variable/constant replacement.
